Test the Markov order of the sessions

Source: R/markov_order_test_htna.R
markov_order_test_htna.Rd

markov_order_test_htna() tests the Markov order of the session sequences of an htna network (or of raw sequence data). The Markov-order test compares the fit of models of increasing order (zero, one, two and so on) with likelihood-ratio statistics, judged against a permutation null, and reports the information criteria of each order. A transition network is a first-order Markov model: the next code is assumed to depend only on the current one. When the next code also depends on the codes before it, a first-order network misses part of the process and a higher order describes it better.

The orders are tested in turn: the selected optimal_order is the highest order reached before the first step that is not significant at alpha, and equals max_order when every step is significant, in which case the search should be widened. The orders preferred by BIC and AIC are reported alongside. markov_order_test_htna() runs Nestimate's markov_order_test() on the sequences and returns a net_markov_order object.

Use it before interpreting a first-order network, together with reliability_htna() and casedrop_reliability_htna() for the stability of the estimated weights.

Usage

markov_order_test_htna(data, ...)

Arguments

data

An htna network from build_htna(), or sequence data (a wide data frame or a list of character vectors).

...

Settings: max_order (default 3), n_perm (permutations, 500), alpha (0.05), parallel (FALSE), n_cores (2), seed and dof ("paths" or "observed").

Value

An object of class net_markov_order with print(), summary() and plot() methods. summary() returns a data frame with one row per tested order and columns order, loglik, AIC, BIC, df, g2, p_permutation, p_asymptotic and significant. The object also holds optimal_order, bic_order and aic_order.

See also

reliability_htna(), casedrop_reliability_htna(), centrality_stability_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
# n_perm = 20 keeps the example fast; use the default 500 in practice.
mo <- markov_order_test_htna(net, max_order = 2, n_perm = 20, seed = 1)
mo
#> Markov Order Test  [within-w permutation, n_perm = 20, alpha = 0.050]
#>   428 sequences / 19346 observations / 12 states
#> 
#>   Selected order  BIC: 1   AIC: 2   permutation-LRT: 2
#> 
#>  order    loglik      AIC      BIC   df       g2 p_permutation p_asymptotic
#>      0 -43741.91 87505.83 87592.40   NA       NA            NA           NA
#>      1 -37315.96 74899.92 75954.53  121 12815.99    0.04761905            0
#>      2 -33812.56 70683.12 82716.72 1272  6481.76    0.04761905            0
#>  significant
#>           NA
#>         TRUE
#>         TRUE
summary(mo)
#>   order    loglik      AIC      BIC   df        g2 p_permutation p_asymptotic
#> 1     0 -43741.91 87505.83 87592.40   NA        NA            NA           NA
#> 2     1 -37315.96 74899.92 75954.53  121 12815.987    0.04761905            0
#> 3     2 -33812.56 70683.12 82716.72 1272  6481.756    0.04761905            0
#>   significant
#> 1          NA
#> 2        TRUE
#> 3        TRUE
